page: Amazon Web Services c6g.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processors utilizing the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The processor configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography enabled. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 12132.72 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5457.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 960.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1519.38. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached reads at 472.95 GB/sec, though uncached large-block reads and writes drop to 124.9 GB/sec and 54.49 GB/sec respectively. The instance demonstrates average performance in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving, but shows weaker results in text processing, compression tasks, and LLM inference.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6g.2xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for ARM-native workloads, delivering dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading overhead. This makes it suitable for multi-threaded applications that benefit from consistent core performance, such as static web serving, software compilation, containerized microservices, and distributed database operations. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, heavy single-threaded processing, or large-scale machine learning inference.
